title: `Mcp-Session-Id`
description: A server-minted session header that binds subsequent Streamable HTTP requests to server-side state.
question: Does this framework return the session header on later requests?
why: Sessions force sticky routing and a shared session store on every deployment. 2026-07-28 removed them outright, so support here is a marker of the older era.
known_issues: Measured with the official MCP conformance suite 0.1.16, whose client scenarios are tagged 2025-11-25.

Also read from the recording proxy's log of every Streamable HTTP session in `scripts/measure_transports.py`: after the proxy mints an `Mcp-Session-Id` on initialize, each later request either carries it or does not. The cell combines that with the suite's session scenario.

notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): every request after initialize carried the minted Mcp-Session-Id. The one rejected request is the SSE GET the client opens before initialize on its second connection (render, then render_result), right after its server/discover probe failed; no session existed yet on that connection. The rule counts it because the first connection had already minted an ID.
